samples.summary: Re-searching before replaceActive rebinds the numeric activeIndex to a different occurrence, so Replace can edit text the user never highlighted
samples.evidence: `replaceActive` now calls `this.search(this.query, this.options)` (line 63) before replacing. `search()` (lines 22-35) keeps the previous `activeIndex` whenever `prevIndex < matches.length`, and otherwise falls back to 0 — it identifies the active match purely by ordinal position, not by (blockId, offset). So when the document changed in a way that shifts the match list, the index silently points at a different occurrence than the one highlighted in the UI (`editor.setSearchMatches(state.matches, state.activeIndex)` was called with the OLD list, docs-find-bar.tsx:80). Example: text "dog cat dog", search "dog", press Next → activeIndex 1 = offset 8 (highlighted). A local or remote insert of "dog " at offset 0 gives matches at 0,4,12; the re-search keeps index 1 = offset 4, so Replace rewrites the FIRST dog instead of the highlighted last one. Symmetrically, if matches shrink below the index, `search()` resets to 0 and Replace hits the first occurrence in the document, potentially off-screen. The stale-offset crash/corruption the diff fixes is traded for a silently wrong-target edit; the two new tests only exercise the single-match case where the index happens to still name the same occurrence.

samples.summary: replaceAll now silently replaces occurrences the user was never shown a count for
samples.evidence: `replaceAll` re-searches at line 86 before the guard and the batch, so the set it rewrites is the document's CURRENT matches, not the set whose count the find bar displayed (`counterText` in docs-find-bar.tsx:183 comes from `matchCount`, last synced by `syncHighlights`). Matches that appeared since the last search — typed locally while the bar is open, or arriving from a collaborator over the CRDT — are rewritten in the same undo unit without ever having been counted or highlighted. It is a defensible reading of "replace all", but the UI promise ("2 of 3") and the mutation no longer agree, and the extra edits are only reversible as part of the whole batch.

samples.summary: Find-bar guards for replace still read stale state, so the new in-method re-search is the only thing preventing an out-of-range replace
samples.evidence: `handleReplace` gates on `state.activeIndex < 0` (line 134) and `handleReplaceAll` on `state.matches.length === 0` (line 143); both buttons are additionally disabled from the React `matchCount` mirror. All three values are snapshots from the last `syncHighlights()` and are stale exactly in the scenario the diff targets (document mutated while the bar is open). They are now merely redundant with the new leading `search()` in the model — but the converse case is not handled: when the stale state says 0 matches while the document has acquired some, both buttons stay disabled and Replace/Replace All refuse, so the freshened search never runs. The find bar has no subscription to document changes to refresh `matchCount`, leaving the fix only half-effective from the only production call site.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: `replaceActive` re-searches (find-replace.ts:63) and then indexes `this.matches[this.activeIndex]` (find-replace.ts:66), while `search()` identifies the active match only by ordinal position — keeping `prevIndex` when `prevIndex < matches.length` (find-replace.ts:29-31) and otherwise resetting to 0 (find-replace.ts:33). No (blockId, offset) re-anchoring exists. The UI highlight is painted from the OLD list (docs-find-bar.tsx:80, editor.ts:4047-4050) and nothing re-syncs it on document change: `store.onRemoteChange` (docs-view.tsx:418) only refreshes/renders and clears image selection, and docs-find-bar only re-runs search on query/option change (docs-find-bar.tsx:102-110). So a local or remote edit that inserts/removes an earlier occurrence while the bar is open leaves the ordinal index naming a different occurrence than the highlighted one, and `handleReplace` (docs-find-bar.tsx:132-139) then mutates that wrong occurrence — a silently wrong-target edit on a path reachable in normal collaborative use. The two new tests (find-replace.test.ts:67-101) only cover the single-match case, where the ordinal happens to still name the same match. No guard, no unreachability, and squarely within the correctness lane (wrong result / incorrect mutation), so no refutation ground applies.
